eyebrow: Docker & Deployment for AI Applications · Chapter One
subtitle: Lesson 4 · Docker Fundamentals

code:
docker build -t my-ai-app:1.0 .

#  -t     tags the image with a name and version
#  .      the build context Docker sends along
# "CACHED" next to a step = reused layer, not re-run
caption: COPY . . can only find files inside this build context.

eyebrow: docker run: the flags that matter
caption: -d detached, -p publishes the port, -e sets env, -v mounts a folder.

code:
docker ps                    # list running containers
docker logs -f ai-app        # stream stdout/stderr
docker exec -it ai-app sh    # open a shell inside it
docker stop ai-app           # stop it cleanly
caption: docker exec answers "is it actually there?" without rebuilding anything.

code:
docker run --rm -it my-ai-app:1.0 \
  python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"
caption: Deletes the container the moment it exits — nothing left to clean up.

subtitle: The same loop, for more than one container at a time.
